editorial:
Imagine meeting a brother you never knew existed, only to find out you come from two different worlds that are starting to hate each other. You follow two half-brothers, one Serb and one Croat, who are linked by their mother but separated by borders and beliefs. The movie has a heavy, emotional vibe because it focuses on how family ties can be stronger than political fights. It feels like a slow burn that builds up a lot of tension, making you feel the sadness and the distance between these two men as they both deal with loss and grief.

What really hits hard is how the movie predicts the future. Since it came out in 1988, it feels spooky seeing it guess the war that actually happened a few years later. The acting is grounded and feels real, though the pacing can be a bit slow in the middle. If you enjoy dramas that make you think about history and family, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the two brothers finally face the reality of their connection. Even though the world around them is falling apart due to ethnic hatred and violence, they realize that their shared blood is more important than their nationality. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, showing that while they cannot stop the coming war, their bond provides a small glimmer of hope and humanity in a very dark time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and historical stories.
